nextStoryContext: US-R1-002 fixed the CRITICAL review finding at test/helpers/test-tmpdir.ts:90: process.on('exit', reapOwnDirectories) never fires under `bun test` (confirmed empirically, bun 1.3.13 -- a process.on('exit', ...) probe prints nothing under bun test but DOES print under `bun -e`/plain `bun <script>.ts`), so directories created via createTestTmpdir during real test runs were never reaped and .cam-test-tmp/ grows unbounded within the story's own 1h-stale-prune window. Root-cause fix, confirmed against Bun's own docs (https://bun.sh/docs/test/lifecycle, 'Global Setup and Teardown', the only documented run-wide multi-file teardown mechanism): (1) exported reapOwnDirectories from test-tmpdir.ts; (2) new test/helpers/reap-preload.ts registers a top-level (no describe wrapper) afterAll(() => reapOwnDirectories()); (3) new repo-root bunfig.toml with [test]\npreload = ["./test/helpers/reap-preload.ts"], loaded before every test file in ANY bun test invocation (whole-suite or single explicit path) since bunfig.toml resolves from cwd at runner startup. The exit hook itself was KEPT (harmless second layer for non-test-runner usage, e.g. a direct `bun -e`/script caller), not removed -- both mechanisms are mutually exclusive in practice depending on runtime. The previous acceptance test (test/helpers/test-tmpdir.test.ts's 'reaper' test) was green while the behavior was broken because it spawned `bun -e` (a runtime where exit hooks genuinely DO fire) instead of `bun test`; fixed by SPLITTING it into two tests rather than silently swapping: the bun -e test was renamed to 'exit hook: ...' to make clear it only pins that secondary layer, and a NEW test ('reaper: a directory created via createTestTmpdir during a REAL `bun test` run is removed once that run exits') spawns the actual bun test runner (`Bun.spawn(['bun', 'test', fixturePath], { cwd: REPO_ROOT, ... })`, absolute fixturePath -- confirmed empirically that a relative path without a leading './' is misparsed by bun as a name FILTER not a literal path and errors 'did not match any test files', while an absolute path is always run regardless of filename convention) against a new dedicated fixture, test/fixtures/reap-preload-fixture.ts. That fixture is deliberately named WITHOUT '.test.'/'_test_' in the filename so the repo-wide `bun test` sweep (no args) never auto-collects it as an extra suite test (confirmed: bun's argument-less/directory-glob discovery filters by filename pattern, but an explicitly-given path bypasses that filter entirely -- this is the same convention already established by the pre-existing test/fixtures/init-home-redirect-probe.ts, though that one is a plain script rather than a bun:test file). The fixture creates one directory via createTestTmpdir and echoes `CAM_REAP_FIXTURE_DIR:<path>` to stdout inside a real test() block; Bun's default reporter surfaces a test's own console.log output verbatim (confirmed empirically), so the parent test greps that marker out of the captured child stdout rather than needing extra file-IO plumbing, then asserts existsSync(childDir) === false after the child's `exited` promise resolves -- proving the preload+afterAll teardown actually ran, in the real runner, end-to-end (manually verified outside the test too: `rm -rf .cam-test-tmp && bun test "$(pwd)/test/fixtures/reap-preload-fixture.ts"` leaves .cam-test-tmp/ empty afterward). test/preflight-deps.test.ts's header comment asserted 'no bunfig.toml exists in this repo' as part of an UNRELATED design rationale (avoiding reliance on Bun's undocumented preload FAILURE/abort semantics for that file's own hard-dependency preflight); updated in the same commit per Doc Maintenance since that specific factual premise is now false, while the underlying rationale (preload-throw abort behavior is still undocumented, even with a bunfig.toml now existing for an unrelated success-path afterAll hook) still holds and still governs that file's design -- no test behavior there changed, comment-only. Full bun test: 6068 pass / 0 fail (net +1 vs. the 6067 baseline: the old single 'reaper' test became two). bun run typecheck clean. bun run check:all fully green (file-size, coverage, debt-markers, dead-code, dup, lint, embed-vendor, ci-parity, agents-md, test-sleeps, test-tmpdir, skip-ratchet all ok) with no file-size-budget.json/coverage-budget.json _ref raise needed (all new files are small; file-size-budget.json has no default ceiling, only explicit per-file entries, so untracked new files aren't gated until a future story grows one past a ceiling someone adds). Next agent should check prd.json for the next non-passing, non-operator story after US-R1-002.

officialDocsValidated.summary: Fetched to validate the fix's design before implementing. Docs confirm exactly the intended mechanism under 'Global Setup and Teardown': define beforeAll/afterAll in a separate file, then load it with `bun test --preload ./setup.ts`, or add `[test]\npreload = ["./setup.ts"]` to bunfig.toml to avoid retyping the flag every run. Also confirms afterAll registered outside any describe block is 'Scoped to a Test File' (file-scoped) -- since the preload file is the first thing bun test loads, its scope is effectively the whole run. Live end-to-end verification (not just docs-reading) additionally confirmed: (a) bunfig.toml [test].preload applies whether bun test is invoked against the whole suite or a single explicit file path; (b) console.log output inside a test() body is surfaced verbatim by bun's default reporter, used to pass the created directory's path back to the parent test process without extra file-IO.
